title: Power Apps: calendar and card layouts for views in model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, admin path and CLI operation are supported, and searches did not find controls or licensing specific to the planned layouts. One minor correction should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance about whether Environment Makers need licences to run model-driven apps.

claims.fix: Keep the licensing FAQ requirement, but add: "Microsoft's Share a model-driven app page separately says users assigned the Environment Maker security role don't require licences to use model-driven apps, which conflicts with the licensing FAQ." Link that sentence to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/share-model-driven-app#app-sharing-privilege-and-licensing-requirements.

claims.quote: While Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans, and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter that give premium Power Apps usage rights satisfy the requirement generally, use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.

claims.claim: No Learn documentation for the planned new layouts was found at review time.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "new view layout"; "model-driven" "calendar" "card" "layouts". Opened Understand model-driven app views; read results for Add the calendar control to tables and Create a card form, which describe existing controls, not this planned layout feature.

claims.claim: Detailed data-editing behaviour for the planned layouts is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "model-driven" "new view layout" calendar card edit actions supported tables. Opened Understand model-driven app views; read existing calendar and editable-grid search excerpts; none identifies the planned layouts or their editing behaviour.

claims.claim: The record actions available in the planned layouts are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "model-driven" "new view layout" calendar card edit actions supported tables. Opened Understand model-driven app views; read Work with rows in the calendar view excerpts for the existing Calendar control, not the roadmap's new layouts.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no autonomous capability.
claims.quote: Makers can now choose to display their data as a calendar or a stack of cards instead of the default grid layout.

claims.claim: Existing table security continues to govern model-driven app data.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use role-based security for sharing. The fundamental concept in role-based security is that a security role contains privileges that define a set of actions that can be performed on tables within the app.

claims.claim: Existing column security continues to govern access to model-driven app data.
claims.quote: Column-level security configurations are organization-wide and apply to all data access requests.

claims.claim: Environment grid and view settings are at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Grids and views.
claims.quote: select **Manage**. ... select **Environments**. ... select an environment. ... select **Settings**. ... Expand **Product**, and then select **Features**. ... ## Grids and views

claims.claim: advancedcolumneditorenabled is a writable Boolean organization column controlling display column options on model-driven app views.

claims.claim: The related grid settings and advancedcolumneditorenabled are not documented as controlling the new layouts.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "calendar" "card" "layout" "settings" API organization. Opened Manage feature settings, pac env and Organization table/entity reference; searched the latter for calendar, card and layout. None ties these settings to the planned layouts.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; Governance controls prose; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate tenant or environment UI switch or API for the planned calendar and card layouts was found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "model-driven apps" "calendar" "card" "admin" "enable"; "calendar" "card" "layouts" "Power Platform" "API"; "model-driven" "layout" "calendar" "PowerShell". Opened Manage feature settings, pac env and Organization table/entity reference; no switch found.

claims.claim: The precise app, view or table level at which makers configure the new layouts remains undocumented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "new view layout"; "model-driven" "calendar" "card" "layouts". Opened Understand model-driven app views; read existing Calendar control configuration excerpts. The roadmap names the designer but not the new layouts' configuration level.
